_comment: Judgment rows of the domain-model score - the ones no grep settles. Re-record them by running the /domain-driven-design review and editing this file; editing it IS the re-recording, because scripts/domain-score.mjs measures staleness from when this file was last touched relative to the Core modules. A row is reported stale, and drops out of the verified score, when a Core module was touched more recently. Structural rows are not recorded here: they are re-checked from the tree on every run.
reviewer: /domain-modeling re-record after #129 bounded the strict read-back to the invocation's own record extent (Core trace-sink.ts and trace-verify.ts). The cost: since #126 every strict finalize read the whole shared trace file, so in the documented eval setup (one PI_FLOWS_TRACE_FILE for a run) flow N reread flows 1..N-1 — quadratic I/O whose only product was rows the invocation scoping then skipped. The design question #129 named — a byte offset taken at construction is not a clean boundary because flows interleave — dissolves once the boundary is stated as ownership rather than position: the file is append-only, so the file's size the moment the sink is born divides bytes that predate the invocation (which cannot honestly carry its just-minted random invocation id) from the region any concurrent writer can still touch. The sink captures that size at birth — deliberately not at first write, because appends are queued without awaiting and a stampless row another writer lands ahead of the queued first append must stay inside the extent, or the launder check would turn on a queue race (pinned in tests/trace-extent.test.ts) — and both readings read only from there through one bounded reader (readExtent, trace-verify.ts). Races can only under-estimate the boundary, which reads extra foreign rows: the safe direction, also pinned. Every in-extent verdict is unchanged and the existing pins pass untouched: forged-identity surplus, stampless remainders, co-tenant runs, and the shared-predicate agreement with the report (declaresOwnRoot) all stand. One disclosed delta, pinned and CHANGELOG'd: a stampless remainder already in the file before the flow call began no longer refuses the live gate — it is a predecessor's torn record, the whole-file report's business (the report still refuses the file, asserted in the same test), symmetric with rows appended after finalize, which were always beyond the live verdict. No aggregate, transition, or lifecycle ordering changed: the extent is private closure state of the sink like the invocation id beside it, verifyExportedTrace keeps taking what it needs as arguments because the reader is deliberately not the writer, and no public type moved — so small-aggregates, behavior-rich, domain-events, depth-rich-core, and depth-invariants-in-aggregates stand as re-derived. Language: CONTEXT.md gains Record extent beside Invocation id, with offset and byte range on its Avoid list; code, tests, docs (flow-reference.md), and the CHANGELOG say extent, and no competing vocabulary shipped, so depth-language-consistency stands with its known blemishes unchanged. Prior re-record, retained for the trail: /domain-modeling re-record after #128 moved two coordination actions' evidence into the seams that perform them (Core trace-scope.ts and approval.ts, plus Generic commands.ts and the three mode call sites). The gap: coordination events were hand-placed at 15 sites across 7 mode files, and nothing could tell that a handler forgot one — trace health counts what the sink attempted, so a mode that recorded nothing read as recorded. The angle the issue endorsed is the one child spans already use: recordSpan is unforgettable because its single call site sits inside the seam every run passes through. The two hand-placed kinds with such a seam now mint there: runCheckCommand (Generic, following the shared-write precedent — the assembly rule lives in Core as mintEvent, trace-scope.ts, and Generic invokes it at the one position that knows the outcome) records the validation outcome of every deterministic gate — including a gate that could not start, previously evidence-free on evaluate's refuse-first path — and issueApprovalReceipt (Core) records the approval event carrying receipt identity, so consent becoming a durable receipt is attested where it happens. Both take a required EventAttribution (trace-scope.ts): the caller's event name, span placement, and own facts, plus the recorder or its stated absence — record: undefined is a declared answer, never a fall-through, and deliberately weaker than the child-span model in that a caller can still decline evidence, but must write the declination where review sees it — and the seam's facts merge last through the one mintEvent home so attribution cannot override what happened and a third seam cannot reverse the spread (pinned for both seams in tests/coordination-evidence.test.ts). The hand-placed remainder is state, retry, and the controller-parsed verdict validations; #133 tracks it with the declaration angle #128 left open. Event names, placements, and wire attributes are unchanged, so the existing trace-topology and trace-evidence pins pass untouched. No aggregate, transition, or lifecycle ordering changed: the admission walk and settle sequence are as they were, the receipt verify/consume path is as it was, and the one behavioral delta beyond the new spawn-failed evidence is that the approval event records at issuance rather than after the following persist — evidence of consent no longer depends on the persist landing, the fail-closed direction. So small-aggregates, behavior-rich, depth-rich-core, and depth-invariants-in-aggregates stand as re-derived, and domain-events gains the minted-event mechanism (its note updated). Language: CONTEXT.md gains Minted event beside the Coordination event entry, naming EventAttribution and the deliberate boundary — a mode's own state transitions and retries have no shared seam performing them and stay hand-placed in the handler — with framework event and auto-event on the Avoid list; no competing vocabulary shipped, so depth-language-consistency stands with its known blemishes unchanged. Prior re-record, retained for the trail: the #127 fix touched the Core trace modules trace-sink.ts, trace-verify.ts, trace-report.ts, and trace-scope.ts. The stable trace identity was carrying two jobs: correlating an eval row with its runtime trace (its purpose), and isolating one run's rows on read-back (a job it cannot do, because a traced pre-spawn refusal and the retry after it legitimately share trace context and mode, hence an id - #127's false TRACE_INCOMPLETE against exactly the strict population). The fix separates the jobs instead of widening the identity: each sink call mints a random flow.invocation_id, stamped on the one append path every row leaves through - the invariant lives inside the sink where rows are made, not with any caller, and tests/trace-invocation-scope.test.ts pins that every exported row carries the stamp its link reports - and both readers (the runtime read-back and the report's grouping) judge an invocation only on the rows carrying its own stamp. stableTraceIds is untouched, so the eval linkage the stable identity exists for survives unchanged. No aggregate, transition, or field changed: the discriminator is private state of the sink closure, surfaced on FlowTraceLink as evidence identity, and verifyExportedTrace keeps taking identity as an argument because the reader is deliberately not the writer - so small-aggregates, behavior-rich, domain-events, depth-rich-core, and depth-invariants-in-aggregates stand as re-derived. The fail-closed direction was checked at both readers rather than assumed: one of the run's own rows that loses its stamp lands in the missing count (the trace comes back shorter than declared); a row no invocation claims joins every invocation of its trace id in the report, so stripping a discriminator cannot launder a surplus row past the gate; and the residual - a writer forging both ids - is named in trace-verify.ts where the #127 residual used to be recorded, and pinned by the reworded forged-identity surplus test. Language: CONTEXT.md gains Invocation id beside Trace health and Trace structure, with trace id (the stable eval linkage) and attempt (part of the stable identity) on its Avoid list; code, tests, and docs (flow-reference.md, troubleshooting.md) all say invocation id and flow.invocation_id, and no competing vocabulary shipped, so depth-language-consistency stands with its known blemishes unchanged. The two-axis review round then closed one real gap both axes converged on: the read-back dropped stampless rows while the report counted them against every invocation, so a file holding a pre-discriminator run beside a stamped one under a shared stable id passed the live gate and failed the report - the false refusal relocated one reader downstream. Both gates now decide a stampless remainder through one shared predicate (declaresOwnRoot, in trace-structure.ts where both already import their accessors): a remainder that declares its own root is a whole run from a pre-discriminator writer and is judged as its own; one that does not counts against this run at the live gate exactly as at the report, pinned from both sides in tests/trace-invocation-scope.test.ts. The release validator's duplicate-span and root-reuse keys became invocation-aware for the same collision. The round also named Invocation id as the deliberate carve-out from the Run entry's Avoid list, following the Run state precedent, and gave the sink's append its named ExportRow type.

small-aggregates.label: Aggregates are small (one root + minimal cluster)
small-aggregates.note: Flow (flow.ts) is the aggregate root CONTEXT.md promised: one bounded delegation whose lifecycle is the explicit typed progression refused → admitted → dispatched → settled. The root stays small by owning ordering only — every pre-spawn gate is a supplied predicate/approval object walked in the aggregate's declared order, and Budget, the handoff consumer, and the trace sink remain separate objects the root holds references to. Run (run.ts) is the one root over a child result's lifecycle. index.ts execute() is a composition root again: it adapts ctx/ui/liveFlows/session persistence into the aggregate's ports and hands over (#97). The residue #100 named is resolved: the aggregate carries the one ResolvedCall (post-preset params, policy, preset) and hands it to ports as arguments — resolvePreset is pure, the details builder is constructed once from the resolution, preset formatting comes back from preparation — so no port in execute() assigns a local another port reads (tests/flow-capture-ownership.test.ts).

behavior-rich.label: Domain objects contain behavior, not just data
behavior-rich.note: Budget owns its rule. DelegationContract's transitions live on ResolvedDelegationContract, and receipt consumption exists only on ApprovalAuthorization — the capability verify returns, bound to the verified consumer (PR #98 review). The residue named by #97 is resolved: an envelope or handoff now attaches to a result only through Run.acceptReturnEnvelope / Run.acceptHandoff (run.ts), and what sanitize.ts held as two module-level WeakMap side-channels is now ECMAScript-private state of the one Run object per result, with consume-once semantics (the envelope candidate is capped on capture, discarded on failure, and taken exactly once). This is encapsulation behind domain transitions, not field privacy: FlowRunResult deliberately stays the plain, writable read projection the views and the runner fill (exit codes, usage, durations), and the identity lookup Run.of is itself WeakMap-backed — the difference is that the state and its ordering now live inside one object that owns them. #106 extends the same pattern in both directions. Run's rejected-envelope retention is ECMAScript-private state under the same consume-once discipline (stored as an isolated clone, taken exactly once), and eligibility is deliberately not Run's to decide — delegation.ts decides it, which is why the check ordering that makes the retention safe is documented on the check rather than on the field. Budget absorbed the wrap-up threshold as its own rule (nearsLiveStop, wrapUpNotice) instead of exposing a fraction for callers to compare against: the notice has to name the authority and spend of the ceiling about to bind, so one cascade at a scaled fraction resolves both the notice and the later refusal and they cannot describe different ceilings.

domain-events.label: Events/handoffs carry cross-boundary flow
domain-events.note: Handoff is a real transfer object: validated, redacted, policy-checked, provenance-bearing, and refused rather than silently degraded. CoordinationEvent is an immutable past-tense fact vocabulary over seven kinds. Events are export-only by design — coordination here is synchronous because a flow settles. The seams that perform a coordination action mint their own events (Minted event, #128): the handoff consumer's sites were already framework-minted, and the deterministic gate runner and approval-receipt issuance now join them, each taking a required EventAttribution so a caller without a sink states the absence instead of the evidence being forgettable.

depth-rich-core.label: Depth: the Core Domain is genuinely rich, not CRUD
depth-rich-core.note: Trace evidence is now gated on both questions it raises rather than only the one the writer can answer: export accounting from the sink, and structure from reading the finished file back. That distinction is Core content, not plumbing — CONTEXT.md sells a finding that arrives carrying its own evidence, and a gate that certifies a file no reader can follow sells the claim without the thing. Contract identity by canonical digest, envelope-to-contract binding, artifact digest verification with realpath escape checks, single-use expiring approval receipts with binding digests, compositional injection, budget authority, and trace health kept separate from execution success and from verified outcome success. The admissibility seam adds another, and this review sharpened its mechanism: the selection eval no longer reassembles the tool's pre-spawn gates from imported predicates. Aggregate-level gates are still Core predicates the eval imports (the spawn gate, depth, concurrency, strict-trace config) and workflow's phase rules remain shared Core (validate-workflow.ts), but every per-mode refusal is now declared by the mode that enforces it and resolved through the table (preSpawnRefusalForParams), so the scored gate cannot drift from the enforced one by construction rather than by hand-maintained agreement, and a mode added to the table is covered without the eval changing. What the eval scores stays its own decision, named in one place (SCORED_PRE_SPAWN_CODES) instead of being implied by which predicates it happened to import. The distinction the declarations force is itself domain content: a refusal knowable before dispatch is the mode's declaration, while one only reachable mid-run (a probe that fails to start, a cycle stranding only later waves) stays in the handler and names a different moment.

depth-invariants-in-aggregates.label: Depth: invariants live inside aggregates, not services
depth-invariants-in-aggregates.note: Follows small-aggregates. Flow-level ordering — admission (preset expansion, mode detection, spawn gate, depth, concurrency, preset trust, preset preparation, strict-trace config, project-agent trust, spawn checkpoint, handler resolution, budget construction) and the settle sequence (blocking handoffs → preset formatting → reflexion → finalize checkpoint → trace finalize → strict-trace refusal → persistence last) — is enforced by the Flow aggregate's typed transitions: admission returns the only dispatch capability, dispatch returns the only thing that can settle, and both spend themselves. Rules like 'a refusal after the sink exists finalizes the trace with child_count 0' are internal to the aggregate. Named by tests/flow-lifecycle.test.ts and the checkpoint-skipped-before-spawn / settle-without-dispatch fault-manifest entries.

depth-language-consistency.label: Depth: ubiquitous language is consistent across docs, code, and tests
depth-language-consistency.note: A seventh blemish was found and fixed by the strict-trace review: 'trace health' was doing duty for both how much of the export was written and whether the export is a tree, two questions with different answers and different observers. CONTEXT.md now carries Trace structure beside Trace health with each on the other's Avoid list, and the code keeps them as separate members so neither can be reported as the other. CONTEXT.md carries Avoid lists; code and test names use the glossary's terms. A sixth blemish was found and fixed by the run-state review: the four states queued/running/completed/failed were named identically by three surfaces but derived three ways, so the ubiquitous language held while the derivation behind it forked — the failure mode this row exists to catch, appearing as agreeing words over disagreeing code rather than as competing words. CONTEXT.md now carries Run state, Settled names runSettled/runFailed as the question's one home and records why isFailed keeps a deliberately different contract, and the shared type is re-exported from run.ts rather than declared twice. A fifth blemish was found and fixed by the mode pre-spawn refusal review: that change claimed the bare phrase 'pre-spawn refusal' for a narrow new concept while six existing sites already used it for any refusal before spawning, and it simultaneously shipped 'pre-spawn declaration' as a second word for the same new concept. CONTEXT.md now carries Mode pre-spawn refusal with the bare phrase and the competing word both on its Avoid list, the mode files and the test speak the recorded term, and Mirror is sharpened to say a mirror is a second derivation that must be kept in agreement — preferring a declaration, which removes the second copy. A fourth blemish was found and fixed by the #106 review: #106 shipped the rejected-envelope concept with no glossary entry and under three competing words — 'rejected' (used in delegation.ts for both the always-returned trace evidence and the conditionally-retained Run field, which sit on opposite sides of the Return envelope entry's binding line), 'salvageable' (the discriminator), and 'unvalidated' (the label already shipped in preset-review.ts, troubleshooting.md, and the CHANGELOG). CONTEXT.md now carries Rejected envelope and Unvalidated claims — the outward-facing word won, so no user-visible sweep was needed — and delegation.ts, run.ts, preset-review.ts, troubleshooting.md, and the tests speak them, the discriminator having been renamed salvageable → claimsSurfaceable so the retired word does not survive in the code that retired it. One residue is deliberate: runner-budget.ts's 'distinguish salvage from loss' is the budget wrap-up sense (a run salvaged from forfeiture), not this concept, and is left alone. Three known blemishes remain. (1) 'contract' is overloaded between DelegationContract and RunModeContract. (2) topology.ts is named for mode topology but holds spec-parameter arithmetic, which is why it sits in Generic while the modes it is named after are Supporting. (3) 'the active child' is standard phrasing at 11 occurrences across docs/reference/flow-reference.md, docs/explanation (patterns, privacy-telemetry), docs/how-to/troubleshooting.md, examples, tests, budget.ts, and the schema.ts param descriptions (the README occurrence left with the Diátaxis reorg), though 'active' is on the Live entry's Avoid list; that sweep needs its own change, because fixing a subset breaks the README / flow-reference / TypeBox-params sync rule in AGENTS.md. Consequently budget.ts deliberately holds both vocabularies: the new API it introduces (stopsLiveRun and its JSDoc) takes the glossary term, while the pre-existing user-visible error cause keeps 'active child' so it stays consistent with the docs until they are swept together. Separately, the exported span attributes flow.budget.limit_* in trace-attributes.ts keep 'limit' as wire format - renaming them would break trace consumers, so they are a deliberate carve-out from the Budget ceiling Avoid list, not drift.

foreignImports._comment: adapters: modules where a foreign package type may legitimately be spoken - the anti-corruption layer, the extension registration surface, and the terminal views. debt: modules that still leak a foreign type into the domain and should not, each declaring in `imports` exactly which foreign packages it may name. scripts/domain-score.mjs enforces the ledger against the base revision AND against the tree: a module's actual foreign imports must equal its declared set, a declared package that is no longer imported must be deleted, and neither a new module nor a widened `imports` set may be added. So a new leak has to be fixed rather than recorded, and an existing entry cannot absorb one. The score's ACL row stays failed until the list is empty.
